subject: Polity
description: Discretionary powers of state Governors in India — situational discretion, hung assembly, dissolution, ordinance veto, model code conventions.

questions.stem: When is a state GOVERNOR justified in using DISCRETIONARY POWERS?
questions.explanation: GOVERNOR's DISCRETIONARY POWERS arise in SITUATIONS where the Constitution doesn't bind him to act on Council of Ministers' advice. KEY CIRCUMSTANCES: (1) HUNG ASSEMBLY (no party with majority) — Governor decides which leader to invite to form government. (2) Loss of MAJORITY — Governor can dismiss CM and ask for floor test. (3) Recommendation of PRESIDENT'S RULE under Article 356 — Governor's discretion (in practice, advised by Centre). (4) Reservation of bills for President's consideration (Art 200). (5) Receiving REPORTS from constitutional functionaries. (6) Discretion in administering 5th/6th schedule areas (tribal). (7) Discretion in NE states (e.g., Nagaland — Governor has 'special responsibility' for law-and-order, Art 371A). KEY ARTICLES: Art 163(1) — 'except in so far as he is by or under this Constitution required to exercise his functions or any of them in his discretion' — clear that some discretion exists. ROUTINE FUNCTIONS — Governor MUST act on CABINET ADVICE per Article 163: bill assent, appointments, etc. NOTABLE CASES: (a) Bommai Case (1994) — limited Art 356 misuse; floor test must precede CM dismissal. (b) Karnataka 2018 — Governor invited single largest party (BJP, no majority); SC ordered immediate floor test. PYQ FREQUENCY: Governor's discretion in UPSC, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Article 163 of the Indian Constitution deals with:

options.option_text: Council of Ministers to aid Governor

questions.explanation: ARTICLE 163 — 'COUNCIL OF MINISTERS to AID and ADVISE the GOVERNOR': (1) There SHALL BE a Council of Ministers headed by CM to aid and advise Governor in exercise of his functions, EXCEPT in so far as the Governor is required to exercise his functions in his discretion. (2) If a question arises whether a matter is one in which Governor must use discretion — Governor's decision is FINAL and CANNOT BE QUESTIONED IN COURT. (3) Question of whether ministers gave advice CANNOT be inquired into in any court. KEY: Art 163 is ANALOGOUS TO ART 74 for the President at Centre — but PRESIDENT has FAR LESS discretion (74 was AMENDED in 1976 + 1978 to make presidential aid-and-advice BINDING; Art 163's wording for Governor is somewhat MORE FLEXIBLE). RELATED ARTICLES: (a) ART 153 — there shall be Governor for each state. (b) ART 154 — executive power of state vested in Governor. (c) ART 155 — appointed by President. (d) ART 156 — holds office during President's pleasure (5 years term but removable). (e) ART 161 — pardoning power. (f) ART 200 — assent to bills (can return non-money bill once for reconsideration). (g) ART 213 — promulgate ordinances. PYQ FREQUENCY: Art 163 in UPSC, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: When a state bill is RESERVED for President's consideration under Article 200, the President has the option to:

options.option_text: Give assent or withhold or return
Send the bill back to bench again
Appoint a Governor for ruling there

questions.explanation: ARTICLE 200 — Governor has 4 options on a state bill: (1) ASSENT (becomes law). (2) WITHHOLD ASSENT (bill dies, but rare — undemocratic). (3) RETURN to legislature for reconsideration (NOT money bill) — if state passes again, Governor must assent. (4) RESERVE for President's consideration (e.g., bills affecting HC powers, related to property acquisition). After RESERVATION (Art 201): PRESIDENT can: (a) Give assent → bill becomes state law. (b) Withhold assent → bill dies. (c) DIRECT GOVERNOR to RETURN to state legislature. State legislature reconsiders; if passes again with/without amendments, sends back to Governor → who reserves for President AGAIN → President's option remains the same. KEY: there's NO TIME LIMIT for President to act on reserved bills — leading to long delays in some cases. CONCERN: bills can sit indefinitely, blocking state legislation. RECENT CONTROVERSIES: (1) TAMIL NADU 2023 — multiple state bills pending at Governor's desk (NEET exemption etc.); SC asked Governor to act 'promptly'. (2) KERALA 2023-24 — Governor sat on bills; CM Vijayan moved SC. STATES WITH MAJOR FRICTION (recently): TN, Kerala, Punjab, Telangana, WB. CONSTITUTION REVIEW COMMITTEE recommended TIME-LIMITS, but not yet enacted. PYQ ANGLE: Governor's bill-veto power tested in UPSC, MPSC, state PSC.

questions.stem: Under Article 213, when can a Governor PROMULGATE AN ORDINANCE?

options.option_text: When state legislature is not in session
Anytime he sees a need to use it
Even when assembly is in session

questions.explanation: ARTICLE 213 — Governor can PROMULGATE ORDINANCES (state-level laws) ONLY WHEN: (1) the state legislature is NOT IN SESSION, AND (2) the Governor is satisfied that immediate action is necessary. ORDINANCE-MAKING is on the ADVICE of Council of Ministers (not pure discretion, but technically Governor's act). KEY CONDITIONS: (a) Bill MUST be placed before legislature within 6 WEEKS of next session — else lapses. (b) Maximum life of ordinance: ~6 weeks + session period (about 7-8 months) before it must be passed as legislation or lapse. (c) PROHIBITED ON: bills that would have required PRIOR PRESIDENTIAL SANCTION (e.g., bills on certain subjects in 7th Schedule); such ordinances also require pre-clearance. ANALOGOUS for CENTRE: PRESIDENT has same power under Article 123. NOTABLE CASES: (1) DC WADHWA case (1986): SC condemned 're-promulgation' of ordinances (without going to legislature) — called it 'fraud on the Constitution'. (2) KRISHNA KUMAR SINGH v. STATE OF BIHAR (2017): SC reaffirmed re-promulgation is impermissible. ORDINANCE 'RAJ': in 1990s-2010s, some governors re-promulgated same ordinance dozens of times — practice now stopped. RECENT: Bihar's 2023 reservation increase via ordinance was challenged. PYQ FREQUENCY: ordinance-making power is a top UPSC, MPSC polity MCQ — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: The S.R. BOMMAI CASE (1994) is associated with which constitutional matter?

options.option_text: Reservation policy in jobs and education

questions.explanation: S.R. BOMMAI v. UNION OF INDIA (1994) — landmark 9-judge SC bench judgment that PUT LIMITS on Article 356 (President's Rule). BACKGROUND: Karnataka CM SR BOMMAI was DISMISSED in 1989 over alleged loss of majority; SC eventually held this dismissal UNCONSTITUTIONAL. KEY HOLDINGS: (1) Floor test of majority must occur on the floor of HOUSE — NOT determined by Governor's subjective opinion. (2) President's Rule under Art 356 is JUSTICIABLE (court can review). (3) Material on which Centre bases Art 356 must be RELEVANT and BONA FIDE. (4) Until Parliament approves, the Assembly is only SUSPENDED, not dissolved — so possible to revive. (5) Federal balance is BASIC STRUCTURE — Art 356 must be used SPARINGLY. (6) SECULARISM is BASIC STRUCTURE — Art 356 can be invoked against state governments violating secularism. IMPACT: misuse of Art 356 dropped sharply after Bommai. Art 356 imposed: (a) ~125 times before 1994. (b) ~30 times since 1994 — and most reviewed by SC. RELATED PRECEDENTS: KESAVANANDA BHARATI (1973) — basic structure doctrine. INDIRA NEHRU GANDHI v. RAJ NARAIN (1975) — election cases. RAMESHWAR PRASAD (2006) — Bihar Assembly dissolution case. PYQ FREQUENCY: Bommai case in UPSC, MPSC, polity GS — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Who appoints the Governor of a state in India?
questions.explanation: ARTICLE 155: GOVERNOR APPOINTED by the PRESIDENT OF INDIA (under his hand and seal). In practice, PM and Cabinet recommend; President formally appoints. ARTICLE 156: tenure 5 YEARS, but holds office DURING PRESIDENT'S PLEASURE — meaning the Centre can REMOVE the Governor at any time. ARTICLE 157: QUALIFICATIONS — citizen of India, age 35+, NOT a member of Parliament/state legislature. ARTICLE 158: emoluments + restrictions — cannot hold office of profit, no other paid employment. KEY APPOINTMENT CONVENTIONS (mostly observed but not legally binding): (1) Governor should ideally NOT be from the SAME state. (2) Outgoing CMs of OTHER states often appointed (controversial). (3) State CM's views should be CONSULTED before appointment. (4) Governor should not be a partisan figure. CONTROVERSIAL APPOINTMENTS — RECENT DEBATES: governors with strong RSS/political backgrounds appointed to opposition-ruled states; alleged conflict with state government. SARKARIA COMMISSION (1988): recommended detailed guidelines for Governor appointment + functioning — non-partisan figures, 5-year fixed term, etc. PUNCHHI COMMISSION (2010): reiterated; recommended state legislature should be consulted. NEITHER FULLY IMPLEMENTED. PYQ FREQUENCY: Governor appointment in UPSC, MPSC, SSC CGL polity 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: In which special situation does the Governor of NAGALAND have extra discretionary powers?
questions.explanation: ARTICLE 371A — special provisions for NAGALAND. Includes the GOVERNOR's DISCRETIONARY responsibility for LAW AND ORDER for so long as 'situation requires'. KEY 371A PROVISIONS: (1) Acts of Parliament re: religious/social practices, customary law, civil/criminal procedure, ownership of land/resources DO NOT APPLY to Nagaland WITHOUT Naga Legislative Assembly's resolution. (2) Governor has SPECIAL RESPONSIBILITY for law and order until determined otherwise by President. (3) Governor's individual judgment — NOT bound by Council of Ministers — in this domain. SIMILAR SPECIAL ARTICLES: (1) Art 371 — special arrangements for Maharashtra, Gujarat. (2) Art 371B — Assam (tribal areas). (3) Art 371C — Manipur. (4) Art 371D — Andhra Pradesh + Telangana (employment, education). (5) Art 371F — Sikkim (special protections for Sikkimese culture). (6) Art 371G — MIZORAM (similar to Nagaland). (7) Art 371H — Arunachal Pradesh (Governor's special law-and-order role). (8) Art 371I — Goa. (9) Art 371J — Hyderabad-Karnataka. CONTEXT: NORTH-EAST states often have UNIQUE histories, ethnicities, autonomy demands → constitutional special provisions. NAGALAND specifically: 1963 constituted as state; 16-point agreement with Centre included this Governor role. PYQ FREQUENCY: Art 371 family in UPSC, MPSC 1-2× per cycle.
